title: "Model Results"
subtitle: "STGNN performance on held-out test data (2011–2018), by experiment"

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import base64
import json
import pathlib
import shutil

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

stgnn_dir = pathlib.Path("../machine-learning-module/results/STGNN")
# Only surface the two experiments we stand behind for this study: both predict
# log IR and both use the cyclical (sin/cos) month encoding rather than naive
# per-month deseasonalisation; the only difference is whether environmental/
# land-use covariates are included (cyclical_seasonal) or the model sees IR
# alone (logIR_only). See the "Which experiments are shown" note below.
experiment_names = [n for n in ["cyclical_seasonal", "logIR_only"] if (stgnn_dir / n).is_dir()]

# test.py only ever writes raw (W, N) arrays to test_predictions.npz — no node
# names, countries, or dates attached. Reconstruct those from the merged
# training CSV the same way choropleth.py does, so experiments that only have
# the .npz (i.e. all of them, going forward) still get the interactive plot.
merged_csv_path = pathlib.Path("../data/interim/machine-learning/SEA_dengue_env_monthly_2011-2018.csv")
N_TEST_MONTHS = 14  # test_months in every OpenDengue STGNN config; see choropleth.py

# Attention HTML files live under machine-learning-module/, outside the docs/
# output dir that gets published to GitHub Pages, so a relative iframe src
# pointing there would 404 once deployed. Copy them into a _files folder next
# to this page's rendered output so they ship as part of the published site.
attention_assets_dir = pathlib.Path("../docs/sea-provinces-study-results_files/attention")

param_labels = {
    "window_size":   "Input window (months)",
    "gat1_hidden":   "GAT layer 1 — hidden dim",
    "gat1_heads":    "GAT layer 1 — attention heads",
    "gat2_hidden":   "GAT layer 2 — hidden dim",
    "gat2_heads":    "GAT layer 2 — attention heads",
    "gru_hidden":    "GRU hidden dim",
    "mlp_hidden":    "MLP hidden dim",
    "mlp_layers":    "MLP layers",
    "batch_size":    "Batch size",
    "dropout":       "Dropout",
    "learning_rate": "Learning rate",
}


def load_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else None


def img_data_uri(path):
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    b64 = base64.b64encode(path.read_bytes()).decode()
    return f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}"


def table_html(df):
    return df.to_html(index=False, border=0, classes="table table-sm table-striped")


def metrics_table_html(metrics):
    rows = [
        ("Huber loss", f"{metrics['test_huber']:.4f}"),
        ("MAE (IR)", f"{metrics['test_mae']:.4f}"),
        ("MSE (IR)", f"{metrics['test_mse']:.4f}"),
        ("RMSE (IR)", f"{metrics['test_rmse']:.4f}"),
        ("Best val loss", f"{metrics['best_val_loss']:.4f}"),
    ]
    return table_html(pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Metric", "Value"]))


def params_table_html(best_params):
    rows = [(label, best_params[key]) for key, label in param_labels.items() if key in best_params]
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Parameter", "Value"])
    df["Value"] = df["Value"].apply(lambda v: f"{v:.6f}" if isinstance(v, float) and v < 0.1 else v)
    return table_html(df)


def loss_curves_html(losses, div_id):
    epochs     = list(range(1, len(losses["train"]) + 1))
    best_epoch = int(np.argmin(losses["val"])) + 1
    best_vl    = float(losses["best_val_loss"])

    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=epochs, y=losses["train"],
        mode="lines", name="Train loss",
        line=dict(color="#2196F3", width=2),
    ))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=epochs, y=losses["val"],
        mode="lines", name="Val loss",
        line=dict(color="#FF5722", width=2),
    ))
    fig.add_vline(
        x=best_epoch, line_dash="dash", line_color="grey",
        annotation_text=f"Best val epoch {best_epoch}<br>loss={best_vl:.4f}",
        annotation_position="top right",
        annotation_font_size=11,
    )
    fig.update_layout(
        xaxis_title="Epoch",
        yaxis_title="Masked Huber Loss",
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1),
        margin=dict(l=40, r=40, t=40, b=40),
        hovermode="x unified",
    )
    return fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=False, div_id=div_id)


def per_country_table_html(ctry_metrics):
    df = pd.DataFrame([
        {"Country": r["country"], "Nodes": r["n_nodes"],
         "MAE": f"{r['mae']:.3f}", "RMSE": f"{r['rmse']:.3f}"}
        for r in ctry_metrics
    ])
    return table_html(df)


def build_test_preds(exp_dir):
    """Reconstruct the {dates, nodes} structure interactive_preds_html expects
    from test_predictions.npz + the merged CSV (mirrors choropleth.py's
    _load_predictions / _node_names)."""
    preds_path = exp_dir / "test_predictions.npz"
    params_path = exp_dir / "best_params.json"
    if not preds_path.exists() or not params_path.exists() or not merged_csv_path.exists():
        return None

    preds = np.load(preds_path)["predictions"]
    if preds.ndim == 3:
        preds = preds.squeeze(-1)
    window_size = json.loads(params_path.read_text())["window_size"]

    df = pd.read_csv(merged_csv_path, usecols=["adm_0_name", "adm_1_name", "year_month", "IR"])
    df["year_month"] = pd.to_datetime(df["year_month"])

    nodes = sorted(df["adm_1_name"].unique())
    countries = df.drop_duplicates("adm_1_name").set_index("adm_1_name")["adm_0_name"]

    test_dates = sorted(df["year_month"].unique())[-N_TEST_MONTHS:]
    W = preds.shape[0]
    pred_dates = test_dates if W == len(test_dates) else test_dates[window_size:]
    if len(pred_dates) != W or preds.shape[1] != len(nodes):
        return None

    pivot = (
        df[df["year_month"].isin(pred_dates)]
        .pivot_table(index="year_month", columns="adm_1_name", values="IR")
        .reindex(index=pred_dates, columns=nodes)
    )

    return {
        "dates": [d.strftime("%Y-%m") for d in pred_dates],
        "nodes": [
            {
                "name": name,
                "country": countries.get(name, ""),
                "actual": pivot[name].tolist(),
                "pred": preds[:, j].tolist(),
            }
            for j, name in enumerate(nodes)
        ],
    }


def interactive_preds_html(test_preds, id_prefix):
    dates             = test_preds["dates"]
    nodes_data        = test_preds["nodes"]
    countries_ordered = sorted({n["country"] for n in nodes_data})
    first_country     = countries_ordered[0]

    trace_list = []
    trace_meta = []
    idx = 0
    for cname in countries_ordered:
        for node in [n for n in nodes_data if n["country"] == cname]:
            visible = cname == first_country
            trace_list.append({
                "type": "scatter", "x": dates, "y": node["actual"],
                "mode": "lines+markers", "name": f"{node['name']} — actual",
                "line": {"width": 2}, "visible": visible,
            })
            trace_list.append({
                "type": "scatter", "x": dates, "y": node["pred"],
                "mode": "lines+markers", "name": f"{node['name']} — pred",
                "line": {"width": 2, "dash": "dash"}, "visible": visible,
            })
            trace_meta.append({"country": cname, "name": node["name"], "ai": idx, "pi": idx + 1})
            idx += 2

    layout = {
        "xaxis": {"title": "Month"},
        "yaxis": {"title": "Incidence Rate (IR)"},
        "title": f"Predicted vs Actual IR — {first_country}",
        "hovermode": "x unified",
        "legend": {"orientation": "v", "x": 1.01, "y": 1},
        "margin": {"l": 40, "r": 180, "t": 80, "b": 40},
        "height": 500,
    }

    _traces_j = json.dumps(trace_list)
    _meta_j   = json.dumps(trace_meta)
    _layout_j = json.dumps(layout)
    _ctry_j   = json.dumps(countries_ordered)
    _first_j  = json.dumps(first_country)

    return f"""
<div>
  <div style="display:flex;gap:20px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;">
    <div>
      <label for="{id_prefix}-csel" style="font-weight:600;">Country:</label>
      <select id="{id_prefix}-csel" style="margin-left:6px;padding:3px 8px;"></select>
    </div>
    <div>
      <label for="{id_prefix}-nsel" style="font-weight:600;">Node:</label>
      <select id="{id_prefix}-nsel" style="margin-left:6px;padding:3px 8px;min-width:220px;"></select>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div id="{id_prefix}-plot" style="width:100%;"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function() {{
  var meta     = {_meta_j};
  var countries= {_ctry_j};
  var traces   = {_traces_j};
  var layout   = {_layout_j};
  var firstC   = {_first_j};

  function init() {{
    var div  = document.getElementById('{id_prefix}-plot');
    var csel = document.getElementById('{id_prefix}-csel');
    var nsel = document.getElementById('{id_prefix}-nsel');

    Plotly.newPlot(div, traces, layout, {{responsive: true}});

    countries.forEach(function(c) {{
      var o = document.createElement('option');
      o.value = c; o.textContent = c;
      csel.appendChild(o);
    }});

    function buildNodeDropdown(c) {{
      nsel.innerHTML = '';
      var all = document.createElement('option');
      all.value = '__all__'; all.textContent = 'All nodes';
      nsel.appendChild(all);
      meta.filter(function(m) {{ return m.country === c; }}).forEach(function(m) {{
        var o = document.createElement('option');
        o.value = m.name; o.textContent = m.name;
        nsel.appendChild(o);
      }});
    }}

    function applyFilter(c, node) {{
      var vis = new Array(traces.length).fill(false);
      meta.forEach(function(m) {{
        if (m.country !== c) return;
        if (node !== '__all__' && m.name !== node) return;
        vis[m.ai] = true;
        vis[m.pi] = true;
      }});
      var title = node === '__all__'
        ? 'Predicted vs Actual IR — ' + c
        : 'Predicted vs Actual IR — ' + c + ' / ' + node;
      Plotly.restyle(div, {{visible: vis}});
      Plotly.relayout(div, {{title: title}});
    }}

    csel.addEventListener('change', function() {{
      buildNodeDropdown(this.value);
      applyFilter(this.value, '__all__');
    }});

    nsel.addEventListener('change', function() {{
      applyFilter(csel.value, this.value);
    }});

    buildNodeDropdown(firstC);
  }}

  function waitForPlotly(fn, n) {{
    if (window.Plotly) {{ fn(); return; }}
    if (n <= 0) {{ console.error('Plotly not available'); return; }}
    setTimeout(function() {{ waitForPlotly(fn, n - 1); }}, 100);
  }}
  waitForPlotly(init, 50);
}})();
</script>
"""


def build_experiment_block(name):
    exp_dir      = stgnn_dir / name
    metrics      = load_json(exp_dir / "metrics.json")
    best_params  = load_json(exp_dir / "best_params.json")
    losses       = load_json(exp_dir / "train_val_losses.json")
    ctry_metrics = load_json(exp_dir / "per_country_metrics.json")
    test_preds   = load_json(exp_dir / "test_predictions.json") or build_test_preds(exp_dir)

    safe_id = name.replace("_", "-")
    sections = [f'<h3 style="margin-top:0;">{name}</h3>']

    if metrics is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Test Set Metrics</h4>
{metrics_table_html(metrics)}""")

    if best_params is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Hyperparameters</h4>
{params_table_html(best_params)}""")

    if losses is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Training Curves</h4>
{loss_curves_html(losses, f"{safe_id}-loss")}""")

    if ctry_metrics is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Per-Country Metrics</h4>
{per_country_table_html(ctry_metrics)}""")

    if test_preds is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Predictions vs Actuals — Interactive time-series</h4>
{interactive_preds_html(test_preds, f"{safe_id}-ts")}""")

    scatter_uri = img_data_uri(exp_dir / "scatter.png")
    if scatter_uri is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Scatter Plot</h4>
<img src="{scatter_uri}" width="700" style="max-width:100%;" alt="Predicted vs actual scatter for {name}"/>""")

    choropleth_uri = img_data_uri(exp_dir / "pred_vs_actual.png")
    if choropleth_uri is not None:
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Choropleth Maps — Predicted vs Actual</h4>
<img src="{choropleth_uri}" width="900" style="max-width:100%;" alt="Predicted vs actual choropleth for {name}"/>""")

    attn_graph = exp_dir / "attention_graph_interactive.html"
    attn_shift = exp_dir / "attention_shift_interactive.html"
    if attn_graph.exists() and attn_shift.exists():
        exp_assets_dir = attention_assets_dir / name
        exp_assets_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(attn_graph, exp_assets_dir / attn_graph.name)
        shutil.copyfile(attn_shift, exp_assets_dir / attn_shift.name)
        rel_graph = f"sea-provinces-study-results_files/attention/{name}/{attn_graph.name}"
        rel_shift = f"sea-provinces-study-results_files/attention/{name}/{attn_shift.name}"
        sections.append(f"""
<h4>Attention Mechanism</h4>
<div class="panel-tabset">
<p><strong>Attention Graph</strong></p>
<iframe src="{rel_graph}" width="100%" height="820px" frameborder="0"
  style="border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #dee2e6;"></iframe>
<p><strong>Attention Shift</strong></p>
<iframe src="{rel_shift}" width="100%" height="820px" frameborder="0"
  style="border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #dee2e6;"></iframe>
</div>""")

    body = "\n".join(sections)
    return f'<div class="experiment-block" id="exp-{safe_id}" data-experiment="{name}" style="display:none;">{body}</div>'


experiment_blocks = "\n".join(build_experiment_block(name) for name in experiment_names)
experiment_options = "".join(f'<option value="{name}">{name}</option>' for name in experiment_names)
first_experiment = experiment_names[0]
```

## What is the SEA Provinces Study?

The **SEA Provinces Study** examines dengue incidence rate prediction at the admin-1 (province) level across 10 Southeast Asian countries. The study uses a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (STGNN) to model the temporal dynamics of dengue incidence while leveraging spatial relationships between provinces. We experiment with a number of message passing configurations to empirically examine both how well and through what mechanism does a model manage to capture whether dengue risk ebbs and flows display interprovincial effects. 

In our final risk index for Southeast Asia, we use the same learned temporal and spatial patterns to generate a risk index for each province, which can be used to inform public health interventions and resource allocation.

Notes:
The gap of incomplete incidence data between 2019 and 2026 is due to a coverage imbalance. To counter act this, the 2011-2018 model will continue to learn and predict between 2019 and 2026, but the predictions will be unvalidated. Thus, interpretation of the latest monthly risk must be done with caution, and the model's predictions should be used as a guide rather than a definitive measure of risk.

## Architecture

The model is a **Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network with GRU** (STGATGRU):

- **Input normalisation:** log1p target transform, then standard-scaled (mean/std from training data); calendar seasonality is supplied as sin/cos month-of-year features rather than removed from the target (see the experiment descriptions below)
- **GAT layer 1:** Spatial message passing over the admin-1 adjacency graph
- **MLP:** Node-wise feature transformation
- **GAT layer 2:** Second spatial aggregation pass
- **GRU:** Temporal sequence modelling over a sliding window (window length is a per-experiment hyperparameter — see each experiment's Hyperparameters table below)
- **Linear head:** Single-step incidence rate prediction (inverse-transformed at output)

Missing admin-1 nodes (no reported incidence) receive a learnable missing embedding
rather than zeroed features, and the GRU hidden state is carried over without update
for those nodes.  Loss masking excludes missing targets from the gradient.

## Bias Correction Note

When the climate-only model runs on current data (post-2018), a climate delta
correction is applied before features are passed to the model.  The delta is
observational: for each variable and calendar month, the 2019–2026 mean of the
same ERA5-Land / CHIRPS / MODIS products minus the 2011–2018 training-period mean.
This shifts current observations back into the model's training feature
distribution, so the risk index reflects how unusual a month is for today's
climate rather than the long-term shift itself.  See
[site/scripts/apply_climate_delta.py](https://github.com/chuang-lab-DMPTD-TMU/dengue-fever-EWS/blob/main/site/scripts/apply_climate_delta.py)
for implementation.

## Experiment Results

We show two experiments here: **`cyclical_seasonal`** and **`logIR_only`**.
Both predict log incidence rate (log IR), both encode calendar month with the
sin/cos cyclical encoding (rather than subtracting a fixed per-month training
baseline — see the [Bias Correction Note](#bias-correction-note) above for why
that matters beyond the training window), and both give missing admin-1 nodes
a learned trainable embedding rather than zeroed-out features (see
[Architecture](#architecture) above). The only substantive difference between them
is input features: `cyclical_seasonal` includes climate and land-use
covariates alongside lagged IR, while `logIR_only` is a purely autoregressive
baseline that sees IR (plus the month encoding) and nothing else — it exists
to quantify how much the environmental features actually buy us over and
above the signal already present in lagged incidence.

Each experiment below is a distinct config/training run under
`machine-learning-module/results/STGNN/`. Pick one to see its metrics,
hyperparameters, training curves, and available plots — sections a given
experiment's artifacts don't include (e.g. attention plots, per-country
breakdown) are omitted for that experiment.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import HTML

HTML(f"""
<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-2.35.2.min.js" charset="utf-8"></script>
<div style="margin-bottom:16px;">
  <label for="exp-sel" style="font-weight:600;">Experiment:</label>
  <select id="exp-sel" style="margin-left:8px;padding:4px 10px;min-width:260px;">
    {experiment_options}
  </select>
</div>
<div id="experiment-container">
{experiment_blocks}
</div>
<script>
(function() {{
  var sel  = document.getElementById('exp-sel');
  var cont = document.getElementById('experiment-container');

  function showExperiment(name) {{
    cont.querySelectorAll('.experiment-block').forEach(function(block) {{
      var active = block.dataset.experiment === name;
      block.style.display = active ? 'block' : 'none';
      if (active && window.Plotly) {{
        block.querySelectorAll('.js-plotly-plot').forEach(function(el) {{
          Plotly.Plots.resize(el);
        }});
      }}
    }});
  }}

  sel.addEventListener('change', function() {{
    showExperiment(this.value);
  }});

  showExperiment('{first_experiment}');
}})();
</script>
""")
```
